title: Tenant-aware cross-region surge fallback and escalation procedure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Create a tenant-aware runbook and escalation procedure to mitigate cross-region outages and large traffic surges that affect hosted and dedicated customers differently. Scope covers detection, automated and operator-driven traffic shifting, tenant-specific fallbacks, customer communications, and post-incident analysis. Excludes on-prem private installs beyond coordination notes (Private teams notified but manual actions required).
background: We observed multiple past incidents where region-level network or infra degradation caused asymmetric impact: hosted customers were routed via fallback regions but suffered higher latencies; dedicated tenants pinned to specific GPU pools experienced hard failures due to region-level control-plane flaps. Existing playbooks are region failover centric and do not encode tenant affinity, quotas, or dedicated tenant isolation needs. This ticket standardizes a tenant-aware approach that: 1) prioritizes SLA-backed dedicated tenants for capacity in fallback regions, 2) avoids cache-warmup storms by throttled warmup, and 3) communicates clear status and remediation steps to impacted customers and internal stakeholders.
runbook_steps:
Detection:
- Alert triggers: region-error-rate > 5% for 5m OR p95 latency spike > 2x baseline for 3m.
- On-call confirms via dashboards: /dashboards/region-health (link below).
Triage:
- Identify affected customer types: hosted vs dedicated vs private using query: SELECT tenant_id,type,region,active_routes FROM tenant_metadata WHERE region = :region.
- If >10 dedicated tenants in region failing, set severity S1 and notify Escalation Channel (#incidents-critical).
Immediate mitigation (automated):
- Activate emergency routing policy (routing-profile: emergency-shift) which moves new traffic to healthy regions respecting tenant routing prefs and capacity tags.
- For hosted traffic, enable model-variant fallback to cheaper variant (model:v1.2-compat -> model:v1.0-compat) to preserve availability.
Operator-driven mitigation (manual):
- For dedicated tenants pinned to region, begin tenant-aware drain: set tenant-routing to 'prefer-fallback' for tenants with SLA tier enterprise. Use api: POST /admin/tenants/:id/reroute body {action: "prefer-fallback"}.
- Throttle rehydrate: use KV-cache prefetch window of 30s staggered across tenants to avoid concurrent KV cache storm.
- Scale up dedicated GPU pools in fallback region if quota available (runbook note: contact sales/ops for reserved expand approvals).
Validation:
- Confirm successful route switch for sample tenants with curl to /health?tenant=:id and verify latency p95 < target and error rate < baseline.
- Watch for increased costs and token rate anomalies; tag incident with cost-alert if projected > 20% over baseline.
communication_playbook:
Internal:
- Post initial incident summary to #incidents-critical and tag SRE, Platform, Oncall Eng manager, and CSMs. Include affected regions, affected tenant count estimate, mitigation actions, and ETA for next update.
- Create incident GitHub issue (template: incident-runtime) linking this Linear ticket.
Customer comms:
- For Dedicated enterprise tenants: CSM to open priority 1 communication indicating degraded region and planned failover. Provide per-tenant timeline and whether manual acceptance is required.
- For Hosted customers: status page update (status.redwood.ai) with affected region and recommended mitigations; follow with targeted email to customers with traffic anomalies observed (list generated by query in runbook).
- Use standardized template (link in Links) and include contact for escalation: oncall+incidents@redwood.ai.
rollback_criteria:
Rollback automated routing if: region-error-rate < 0.5% for 10m AND p95 latency returns within 1.2x baseline for 10m.
- Rollback must be staged: first return hosteds with canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% across 10m windows.
- For dedicated tenants, do not auto-move back; require tenant coordinator to approve and schedule tenant drain windows to repopulate original region.
- Record Rollback decision and approver in incident issue.
monitoring_queries:
Region error rate: sum(errors) / sum(requests) by region over 5m.
P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by region.
Affected tenants list: SELECT tenant_id, tier, region, last_30m_errors FROM tenant_incidents WHERE region = ':region' ORDER BY last_30m_errors DESC LIMIT 250.
KV cache warmup rate: rate(kv_cache_prefetch_events[1m]) by region.
Escalation thresholds are set as Grafana alerts: region_error_rate_high, p95_latency_regional_spike, dedicated_pool_degradation.
postmortem_todo:
Post-incident tasks:
- Collect timeline (SRE + oncall) and publish within 48h.
- Run tenant-impact spreadsheet and send to Sales/CS for customer notifications and compensation considerations.
- Action items: policy engine: add tenant-weighted routing (eng PR); autoscaler: add soft-quota for dedicated pool burst; console: surface per-tenant failover history.
- Owner assignments: timeline doc owner = Diego Alvarez; customer impact spreadsheet owner = Priya Nair; follow-up tasks tracked as sub-issues.
- Schedule blameless postmortem meeting within 7 calendar days.
